prompt: At a grocery store, $30\%$ of customers use a coupon, independently of one another. Of the next $100$ customers, let $X$ be the number who use a coupon. What is the standard deviation of $X$? Round to two decimal places.
hint: The count of coupon users among $100$ independent customers is binomial, and a binomial variable has its own formula for standard deviation.

hints.text: The count of coupon users among $100$ independent customers is binomial, and a binomial variable has its own formula for standard deviation.
Use $\sigma_X = \sqrt{np(1-p)}$. Work out the variance $100(0.3)(0.7)$ first and then take its square root.
$100(0.3)(0.7) = 21$ and $\sqrt{21} \approx 4.58$, so the standard deviation is about $4.58$ customers.

explanation: $X$ counts successes among $100$ independent customers, so it is binomial with $n = 100$ and $p = 0.3$.
The variance of a binomial variable is $np(1-p) = 100 \times 0.3 \times 0.7 = 21$.
The standard deviation is $\sqrt{21} \approx 4.58$ customers. The mean is $30$, so typical counts land within about $4.6$ of $30$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Build it from one customer
steps: One customer is a 0/1 variable with variance $p(1-p) = 0.21$.
SD $= \sqrt{21} \approx 4.58$. That is exactly where the formula $\sqrt{np(1-p)}$ comes from.
